Itochu — investment research portal with auto-built agents.

The Ask

What the user is doing today and what the portal replaces.

The Machinery division produces 120-page Japanese-language slide decks to evaluate M&A targets. Every division does a variant of this. The pain is universal across Itochu's seven divisions; the portal is designed to be the universal answer.

Today · Manual workflow

120-page deck per target, one analyst at a time.

⌧ VDR sealed offOutside Itochu's network
∻ Private data fragmentedNo clean API in-house
⧗ Analyst time bottleneckQuality varies by analyst
⇌ Format drifts per passDeep-dives never align
Proposed · NeuralSeek portal

One portal. Drop in VDR docs. Auto-built research agents. Decks out the back.

⇪ Drag & drop VDRNo direct VDR API needed
☑ Pre-built agent libraryEmployees · revenue · ownership
✦ NL agent builderNeuralSeek code-gens NTL flow
⤓ Bilingual deck outJA & EN · Itochu standard format
Portal Anatomy

Four moving parts.

The portal is one user-facing surface backed by four discrete capabilities. Each is independently testable, and each maps to an existing NeuralSeek pattern we've shipped elsewhere.

Pillar · 01

VDR ingest surface

Drag-and-drop document upload from the seller's data room. No direct VDR integration. Files land in the tenant, get OCR'd, classified, and become first-class context for the agents.

drag_and_drop ocr · classify tenant_scoped
Pillar · 02

Pre-built agent library

~50–100 standard research agents shipped on day one: employee count, revenue, ownership, leadership, capital structure, geo footprint, etc. The "every deck needs these" baseline.

50–100 agents checkbox_select governed
Pillar · 03

NL → agent generator

User types what they want in plain language. NeuralSeek code-gens NTL into a complete flow on the back end. User sees an "agent"; the visual node graph is generated, governed, and audit-logged behind it.

codegen → ntl audit_logged guardrails_on
Pillar · 04

Reusable agent repo + deck output

Good custom agents become reusable across divisions. Final output: an Itochu-format slide deck in Japanese and English, generated in parallel — not translated after the fact.

cross_division format: pptx ja · en parallel
User Flow

Three steps, one workflow.

The portal is one screen with three working areas, plus a quiet feedback loop. The analyst selects a target, picks pre-built agents from the library (groups or individuals), and — if nothing in the library fits — describes a new agent in plain language that gets compiled into a governed NTL flow and added to the Itochu library for the next analyst.

The Differentiator

The user types prose. We compile NTL. The agent appears.

Instead of pre-defining a thousand specific research agents we will never use, we give the user the ability to describe one in natural language and code-gen the NTL flow behind it. Same pattern we already deliver in the robotics-prospecting portal and the KYC / Dun & Bradstreet visualization — applied to Itochu's investment-research surface.

user_request: "agent that researches geopolitical
automobile regulations in Europe"
compiled_to: ntl-flow-2026.05.13-eu-auto
nodes: seek · web_scrape · semantic_score
guardrails: 118 customizable · enforced
audit_lineage: policy_ref + run_id
reusable: published_to_repo
